newsitem.title: FIJI: Striking Fiji sugar workers to return to work.
newsitem.headline: Striking Fiji sugar workers to return to work.

text.p: Fiji's sugar industry workers will return to work late on Tuesday night to end their 16-day strike, their union leader said on Tuesday.
The members of the Fiji Sugar and General Workers Union had reluctantly agreed to resume work, union secretary Felix Anthony told reporters.
Suva's High Court on Monday ordered the 2,500 workers at Fiji's four sugar mills to obey an order by the Fiji Sugar Tribunal to return to work or face contempt of court charges.
Anthony said the union will continue to pursue its demands with the Fiji Sugar Corp (FSC) before the tribunal.
The strike started on July 21 over occupational health and safety concerns at the sugar mills.
Before the strike, Fiji's 1997 raw sugar production was forecast at 440,000 tonnes, down from 475,000 in 1996.
The Fiji Sugar Commission said all harvested cane not crushed after the strike was called will be accepted by the FSC.

Commission chairman Gerald Barrack said growers will be paid for the estimated quantity and value of cane at the start of the strike. Burnt cane will also be accepted, he said in a statement on Tuesday.
